items.title: The space rocket I could have been aboard explodes: Rhiannon Adam’s best photograph
items.summary: ‘I was chosen to go around the Moon on a SpaceX starship. Preparations took over my life. Then, four minutes into watching a rocket on a test flight, it broke apart. And that was the end of my adventure’ This photograph was taken on 20 April 2023 from the VIP section of SpaceX’s launch viewing area, looking out from South Padre Island, Texas, towards Boca Chica, a nature reserve near the Mexican border which is home to SpaceX’s Starbase launchpad. In 2021, I and seven other civilians were selected from an open call to go around the Moon on a free SpaceX Starship flight funded by the Japanese billionaire Yusaku Maezawa. The dearMoon Project included myself and another photographer. For me, the story also became about being plucked from obscurity and planted in this very surreal world I could never have imagined being a part of in a million years. At the time, only 24 white American men had orbited or landed on the moon. Being selected for something like that changes your life and your perception of your worth in the world. The flight, originally scheduled for 2023, completely took over my life. It took the air out of every room – I couldn’t talk about anything else. People stopped commissioning me because they assumed I was busy going to space; every conversation I had was about it. This was going to be the rest of my life. That day in April was pivotal. We were there to watch SpaceX’s Integrated Flight Test 1. After four minutes, following a relatively successful liftoff, the vehicle experienced what they call in space terms an “RUD” – Rapid Unscheduled Disassembly – and broke apart in the air. We put on a brave face but secretly I was thinking: “Wow, the risks are no longer theoretical. I could have been on that.” The dust cloud in the image emerged from the concrete launchpad and tower – obliterated by the power of the raptor engines. The debris ended up all over the local houses and SpaceX closed the launch facility for reconstruction for four months while they conducted a huge clean-up operation. Going to space feels futuristic and grandiose but there are still the practical problems – like people wiping dust off their windows. Continue reading...

GLP-1 blockbuster medications such as Novo Nordisk’s Ozempic and Eli Lilly’s Mounjaro have revolutionised obesity and diabetes treatment but there has been a greater focus by companies on weight loss, according to a report from the Netherlands-based non-profit group. items.title: What happens to your brain when the days get darker? - video
items.summary: As the nights draw in, many of us can experience low mood. But for a small proportion of people a more intense depression develops through the winter months. It’s a phenomenon that since the 1980s has been labelled seasonal affective disorder, or Sad, and can be debilitating for sufferers. To find out more about the latest scientific understanding of Sad, Ian Sample speaks to Russell Foster, professor of circadian neuroscience at the University of Oxford. He explains what scientists think the mechanism for the condition could be and what the evidence says about the best way to tackle it. articles.snippet: 폐 이식을 애타게 기다리다 아내를 먼저 떠나보낸 남편이 마지막 순간 세 사람에게 장기기증으로 새 삶을 선물한 뒤 아내 곁으로 떠났다.한국장기조직기증원은 지난달 8일 분당서울대병원에서 이청룡 씨(68)가 뇌사 장기기증으로 간과 양측 신장을 기증해 3명에게 새 생명을 선물했다고 12일 밝혔다.이 씨는 지난 9월 23일 자택에서 넘어진 뒤 이상 증세를 보여 병원으로 이송됐다. 외상성 뇌출혈 진단을 받고 중환자실에서 치료받았으나 상태가 악화해 끝내 뇌사 판정을 받았다.이 씨의 자녀들은 아버지의 평소 성품과 폐 이식을 기다리다 세상을 떠난 어머니를 떠올리며 장기기증을 결심했다. 이 씨의 아내는 2011년 간질성 폐질환을 진단받았고 2021년 병세가 악화하면서 폐 이식 대기자로 등록됐다. 그러나 끝내 이식을 받지 못한 채 올해 2월 세상을 떠났다.아들 승선 씨는 어머니가 돌아가셨다는 소식을 듣고 집을 나설 준비를 하던 중, 어머니가 다니던 병원에서 기증자가 나타났다는 연락을 받았다.

articles.snippet: 청와대는 12일 미국 중간선거가 전시작전통제권(전작권) 환수 협의에 미칠 영향과 관련해 “중간선거 관련 영향은 아직 특별히 가시화된 것은 없다”고 밝혔다.청와대 고위 관계자는 이날 오전 춘추관에서 기자들과 만나 미 중간선거 영향으로 전작권 환수 협의에 차질이 빚어질 수 있다는 관측을 묻는 질문에 “고위급, 장관급도 그렇고 정책실장급에서도 그렇고 논의는 조금씩이나마 진전되고 있다”며 이같이 밝혔다.이 관계자는 최근 한미 국방장관 협의와 국방부 정책실장의 방미 협의를 언급하며 “전작권도 논의 사항 중 하나였는데 논의가 잘 되고 있다”고 말했다.그러면서 “정부 대 정부 협의가 중요하고 거기에 집중하고 있다”고 했다.[서울=뉴시스]

articles.title: ‘농어촌기금 출연 기업 노력 의무화’ 여권 단독 처리
articles.snippet: 국회 농림축산식품해양수산위원회가 11일 농어촌상생협력기금 출연에 대한 기업의 노력 의무를 명시한 ‘한미 자유무역협정(FTA) 체결에 따른 농어업인 등의 지원에 관한 특별법’을 여권 주도로 처리했다. 국민의힘은 농협중앙회장 선거를 조합원 직선제로 전환하도록 한 농협법 개정안 처리에 반발하며 이날 회의에 불참했다. 국회 농해수위는 이날 오후 국회에서 전체회의를 열고 FTA 농어업법을 여권 단독으로 의결했다. 내년 종료될 예정이었던 기금 조성 기간을 10년 연장하고 일정 수준 이상 FTA로 수혜를 보는 기업들에 매년 기금을 출연하도록 노력 의무를 부과하는 것을 골자로 한다. 농어촌상생협력기금은 FTA 이행으로 피해를 입은 농어업인의 지속가능한 발전과 농어촌·민간기업 간 상생협력 촉진을 위한 사업을 추진하기 위해 2017년 조성됐다. 10년 동안 매년 1000억 원, 총 1조 원 모금을 목표로 했지만 10년이 지난 올해까지 모금액이 목표치의 3분의 1 수준인 3255억 원에 그쳤다.

articles.title: Does M John Harrison’s Booker win mean science fiction is finally accepted by a ‘snobby’ literary establishment?
articles.snippet: Kazuo Ishiguro, Jeff VanderMeer, Olivia Laing and other writers weigh in on the publishing world’s genre wars As M John Harrison was announced as the Booker prize winner on Monday evening, the 81-year-old looked gobsmacked. Decades into his career, and long overlooked by the mainstream literary establishment, he had just won a prize that has never before rewarded a writer known for science fiction, with a decidedly fantastical book. His fans, many leading authors among them, are thrilled. “For decades it was a standard – and correct – nerd whine to point out that sentence for sentence, book for book, Harrison was one of the greatest writers out there, full stop, but that ‘mainstream’ prizes never reflected that,” says China Miéville, who last week won the Goldsmiths prize with his 1,200-page speculative novel The Rouse. Back in 2002, Miéville wrote that Harrison not having won a Booker by that point proved “the bankruptcy and back-slapping generic snobbery of the literary establishment”. Now, he says: “I am so delighted, for Harrison, and for fiction.” Continue reading...
